page: Amazon Web Services m5n.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture, presenting 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core for a total of 8 vCPUs. Memory capacity stands at 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 vector extensions with VNNI, AES cryptographic acceleration, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache.

Storage and acceleration configurations are lean: the instance includes zero GPU accelerators and has no bundled local ephemeral storage. All operating system and application storage requirements must be addressed via network-attached volumes. To support data transfer demands, the m5n.2xlarge provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation, distinguishing the 'n' variant from standard general-purpose instances.

Empirical benchmarks indicate mid-tier performance across multi-threaded operations and data manipulation. Multi-core stress-ng scores reach 6,766.72 and PassMark CPU reaches 7,642.03, alongside memory read bandwidth reaching 49.53 GB/sec on large uncached blocks. Application tests demonstrate steady throughput, recording 6.78 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.09 GB/sec in static web serving. Conversely, single-thread metrics such as Geekbench single-core (1,123.0) and medium 7B LLM inference processing (9.86 tokens/sec) rank in lower performance brackets.

In terms of cost efficiency, the configuration avoids premium hardware add-ons like local NVMe arrays or GPU accelerators while providing dedicated compute cores and elevated network bandwidth. The primary tradeoff is moderate per-core speed. The instance profile aligns with distributed web serving, microservices, in-memory caching systems, intermediate database tiers, and continuous integration workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services m5n.2xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual server designed for balanced compute and memory tasks with enhanced network throughput. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz across 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs, it includes 32 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and does not include a GPU accelerator, relying on network-attached storage while providing an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations reflect mid-tier performance across multi-threaded operations, including PassMark CPU tests and Redis SET throughput reaching 6.78 million operations per second, though single-core compute and intensive LLM inference remain comparatively modest. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile offers balanced resource distribution without the overhead of unused accelerator hardware, making it well matched for web serving, microservices, mid-sized database tiers, and CI/CD pipelines.
